From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@nimbushealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet coverage scenarios + deal handoff (weekly)

Team — kicking off this week's capacity planning thread for the Nimbus Health pilot / reserved commit discussion. High level: Elaine's pilot is scheduled to start in late June and they are explicitly asking for burst guarantees for Q3 while they scope a reserved commit. We need to run through three coverage scenarios and land on a recommended staging of capacity + burst policy by EOD Monday so sales can finalize the mutual action plan.

Quick asks: 
- Ben: updated close probability and realistic start date for each milestone in the attached MAP (I marked the dates we discussed on the call).
- Laura: cost/carveout scenarios (1) pilot only burst credits, (2) 6mo reserved with credits, (3) 12mo committed pool. Need unit economics for each.
- Karthik: infra constraints for burst slots if we allocate NIM pilot to west-us pools vs dedicated-queue. Also give an ops runbook for pre-warming + KV cache priming for the demo flows.

Attached: fleet_coverage_scenarios_v3.xlsx (skeleton scenarios). I've included the pipeline rows for Nimbus and two other nearby deals that could overlap (see sheet "overlap").

I propose we discuss blockers in the 11:00 standup and aim to publish a short recommendation to Elaine by Monday COB.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Attachment: fleet_coverage_scenarios_v3.xlsx (xlsx spreadsheet, 450KB, contains scenario tabs and GPU counts)

Thanks Rachel — quick data from my side:
- Nimbus Health (NIM-2027-Q3-PILOT): pilot start 2027-06-24 (demo week 6/21-6/25), pilot volume estimate: 600k tokens/day peak, average 180k/day. Probability to convert to commit: 45% (standard risk: procurement has longer cycles).
- Overlap deals: HealthBytes POC (closing 6/30, low velocity) and CardioGen pilot (mid-July, 30% chance) — both use west-us.

Suggested rough sizing (A100-eq slots):
- Pilot burst needs: 12 slots for peak windows (3x baseline concurrency); sustained pilot baseline: 4 slots.
- If pilot converts to 6mo reserve: recommend 40 slots reserved (gives headroom for model upgrades & embeddings workloads).

I'm attaching the MAP I've been using in the forecast. If we carve burst credits instead of raw slots we can cover peaks without immediate reservation but finance/ops have to agree on credit burn rules.

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet coverage scenarios + deal handoff (weekly)

Appreciate the detail. I ran the three scenarios and added a simple unit econ table to fleet_coverage_scenarios_v3.xlsx (sheet: finance_summary). Highlights: 
- Pilot + burst credits (3 months): Negative margin on pilot months (-8%) but reasonable CAC-to-LTV if conversion happens quickly.
- 6mo reserved (40 slots): Improves gross margin to +14% vs hosted baseline, payback 5.8 months if they hit forecasted throughput.
- 12mo reserved (40-60 slots graduated): Best unit economics long-term (+24% margin) but requires stronger legal and SSO/KMS gating (procurement pushback likely).

Questions for ops: if we recommend 40-slot reserve, what's the realistic lead time and how much of that must be cold-provisioned vs burst? Also document the fallback: if capacity hits 85% we route to compatible quantized variant to preserve latency SLO.

I'll flag the 6mo recommendation as our preferred commercial option pending infra confirmation.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet coverage scenarios + deal handoff (weekly)

Quick ops reality: 
- West-US pools currently have ~120 A100-eq equivalent slots usable for production in our dedicated pool. Average utilization across reserved deals is 62%. We can absorb a 40-slot reserve request but it will push peak margin into tight territory for July if CardioGen also ramps. Lead time for firm reservation provisioning (cold) is ~3 weeks (hardware + provisioning), but we can pre-warm software infra within 48-72 hours.
- Burst credits model: we can implement a credits overlay that caps token spend per-client per-24h window and allows burst beyond reserved capacity for X hours, but it requires a new billing rule and a small gating change in the router (2-3 engineer-days).

Ops ask: if we go with 40 reserved slots, please confirm date they'd like the commit live and whether they require region lock (west-us). If they want 60 slot graduated plan we should start hardware procurement now.

Runbook note (will add to wiki): pre-warm steps, KV priming, prefix caching, and a cold-start checklist for demo week.

- Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@nimbushealth.ai>

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from procurement-side so finance has the right levers: 
- Nimbus prefers a 6mo committed option if it can come with predictable burst credits for unexpected demand spikes. Would Redwood be willing to do a 6mo reserved (40 slots) + 10% monthly burst credit pool baked into the contract at a fixed uplift?
- If procurement needs SSO/KMS in place before committing, timeline is tight but possible (we're ready to accept a milestone-based onboarding schedule).

We'll review the scenario worksheet and come back with an internal decision by EOD Wednesday. If you can mark the sheet with your "ops ready" / "finance ready" flags that will speed up our internal review.

Elaine Park
Dir. of Product Ops, Nimbus Health
elaine.park@nimbushealth.ai
